opening.argument: The segment explains a reported Apple-themed phone scam by showing how an unsolicited call can appear to come from Apple, claim that the recipient has a virus, and create a reason to call back. It identifies that call as a ruse to obtain personal information, including names and bank or credit-card information. The accompanying guidance gives viewers a clear prevention message: do not trust caller ID, call the number back, or provide personal information. That framing establishes consumer education and scam prevention as the segment's purpose.

citations.quote: You're going to get an unsolicited phone call and that caller ID is going to look like it's coming from Apple.
All just a ruse to get you to call back and give out your personal information.
